Key observations from the test image:
- Close-up macro view of an orange/tan plant surface (stalk tissue)
- Black, spiky/hairy fungal structures — these are acervuli with dark setae
- Characteristic of Colletotrichum (Anthracnose) fruiting bodies
- The straw-colored surface suggests stalk tissue

This strongly suggests Anthracnose. Let me check both anthracnose reference images and Tar_spot (which also has black structures).

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Macro close-up of orange/tan straw-colored stalk tissue with numerous **black acervuli bearing dark setae** (spiky bristle-like structures) — the classic microscopic hallmark of *Colletotrichum graminicola*
- **Anthracnose_stalk_rot reference**: Upper-right panel shows stalk interior with black fungal bodies on tan/orange fibrous stalk tissue — matches very well
- **Anthracnose_leaf_spot_top_dieback reference**: Shows leaf spots with brown centers/yellow halos and stalk surface lesions — different presentation
- **Tar_spot reference**: Shows flat, circular raised black stromata on green leaf surface — different from the spiky acervuli in the test image

The fibrous, striated orange/tan surface is clearly stalk tissue, and the black structures with prominent setae are diagnostic acervuli of *Colletotrichum* on stalk tissue = **Anthracnose stalk rot**.
